settings.headline: Pick your procedure.
settings.body: Each procedure has its own collection — the recommended strength, the right format, and the products built for that kind of session.

settings.headline: Generic numbing wasn't built for your appointment.
settings.body: A cream made for "skin numbing" handles every situation the same way. Aesthetic procedures don't work that way. A lip filler appointment asks something different from a session of full-face laser. Senseless is built for the procedure, not the average — three strengths, three formats, formulated to match what each kind of appointment actually demands.

settings.question: What's the difference between Senseless and a regular numbing cream?
settings.answer: Regular numbing creams are formulated for generic skin numbing. Senseless is built for aesthetic procedures specifically — three strengths matched to the demands of different appointments, in three formats across cream, gel, and spray.

settings.question: Which procedures does Senseless cover?
settings.answer: Lip fillers, Botox, microneedling, laser, SPMU, waxing, and aesthetic injections more broadly. Each procedure has its own collection with the recommended strength and format.

settings.question: Can I use Senseless for tattoos?
settings.answer: Senseless is formulated for aesthetic procedures rather than tattooing.

settings.question: Which strength should I choose?
settings.answer: Clinical suits most aesthetic appointments. Advanced for longer or more sensitive sessions. Professional for the most demanding indications. See the strength guide.

settings.question: Is Senseless used in clinics?
settings.answer: Yes. Senseless Professional is developed with practitioners and used in clinics across the UK.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
